goal: Teach frontend-oriented AEM developers how an authored image connects a DAM asset, the Core Image Component, responsive delivery and context-specific alternative text, then define the evidence required to review that contract on the Week 2 Guide Page.

deck_context.source_summary: Class 9 of a seven-week AEM Sites course, delivered Thursday, August 27, 2026. The audience understands Resources, Sling resolution, editable templates, policies, dialogs and persisted properties. This class connects the Week 2 Guide Page practice to asset references, Core Image behavior, accessible alternatives and browser delivery evidence.
deck_context.core_claim: A reliable AEM image is a managed DAM reference delivered through proven component capability, given alternative text according to its purpose in the current context, and verified in the repository, rendered HTML and browser network trace.
canonical_facts: A DAM asset below /content/dam owns its binary, renditions and reusable metadata.
An authored Image component below /content stores a fileReference to the DAM asset instead of copying the binary.
A project proxy can inherit Core Image v3 with sling:resourceSuperType = core/wcm/components/image/v3/image when that version is installed.
Core Image v3 provides browser-native responsive image delivery, lazy loading and authoring controls.
Template authors configure allowed responsive widths and relevant defaults in the component policy or design dialog.
Alternative text depends on the image's purpose in the current page context.
Informative images need a meaningful non-empty alternative; decorative images require an explicit empty alt value.
A missing alt attribute is not equivalent to an explicit empty alt value.
Functional image alternatives describe the action or destination; complex images need a short alternative plus a detailed equivalent nearby.
CSS sizing alone does not reduce transferred image bytes.
Web-Optimized Image Delivery is an AEM as a Cloud Service option; local verification can use the Adaptive Image Servlet and browser network evidence.
Incoming references should be inspected before moving, replacing, unpublishing or deleting a managed asset.

style.name: 技术图谱课件风
style.visual_direction: Sober, information-rich technical atlas blended with academic courseware. Use exact repository paths, component properties, responsive candidates, rendered HTML and evidence states instead of generic corporate cards.
style.color_palette: Warm ivory drafting-paper background, deep navy typography, faint square grid, blue for authoring and output, green for valid content, violet for decision or reference flows, restrained orange for warnings.
style.typography: Large bold modern sans serif headings; crisp sans serif body copy; true monospace appearance for paths, properties, resource types, HTML and request values.
style.texture_and_finish: Flat 2D technical diagrams with fine rules, precise repository, asset, component, browser, accessibility and network icons. No gradients, neon, glass, 3D or photography.
style.deck_consistency: Match the approved sample's palette, typography, grid, density, semantic colors, evidence tags and line weight while varying composition by slide role.

approved_style_reference.fidelity: Match palette, typography, grid, technical density, semantic colors, monospace code treatment and fine-line icon language only; do not copy the exact four-branch decision-tree layout.

slides.intent: Separate the managed DAM asset from the component instance that uses it.
key_points: DAM asset owns binary, renditions and reusable metadata
Page Image component is a separate Resource
fileReference points to the DAM asset path
Context-specific properties remain on the component instance
Asset lifecycle changes can affect every incoming reference

Component policy defines allowed widths and defaults
Verify the installed Core Components version
Extend only for a verified gap; never copy the implementation

slides.title: Alternative text describes purpose in context.
slides.intent: Choose alternative-text behavior from the image's job on the page, not from its filename.
key_points: Informative: describe essential meaning
Decorative: render an explicit empty alt value
Functional: describe the action or destination
Complex: short alternative plus detailed equivalent nearby
Purpose before wording; never default to the filename

slides.title: DAM metadata is a source, not the final decision.
slides.intent: Distinguish reusable asset metadata from the meaning required by a particular page.
key_points: One asset can serve different purposes in different contexts
DAM alternative text can provide a reusable default
Page context may require an author override
Decorative means an explicit empty alt value
Developers provide safe controls; authors confirm meaning

Label metadata as a source and page purpose as the final decision.

slides.title: Responsive delivery lets the browser choose appropriate bytes.
slides.intent: Connect policy widths, generated candidates and the source selected by the browser.
key_points: Policy widths define available responsive candidates
Core Image v3 supplies multiple width sources
Browser chooses for layout and device density
Lazy loading can defer offscreen requests
CSS size is not transferred byte size

slides.title: Verify the Guide Page image contract with evidence.
slides.intent: Turn the session into a repeatable review of the Week 2 practice without depending on a live demo.
key_points: Repository: fileReference resolves to the intended asset
Informative: meaningful non-empty alt
Decorative: explicit empty alt value
Missing or invalid: safe observable behavior
Browser: candidates, selected request and rendered dimensions

local_context.required_background: Build a three-row evidence matrix. Informative row: intended fileReference, non-empty alt and responsive request. Columns must be Repository, Rendered HTML, Accessibility result and Network evidence. Add a maintenance checkpoint to inspect incoming references before asset lifecycle changes.

layout.intent: Make the Week 2 Guide Page review executable from artifacts rather than a live demonstration.

Do not require Cloud Manager or a shared deployment environment.

Verify repository reference, rendered alt state and selected source
